title: Feedback Reef: Annotary Playbook + Microprobes (Aug 2026)
content:
Purpose:
A compact, runnable playbook that turns a noisy heap of feedback into 6 small, prioritized microprobes we can ship in 1–3 sprints. Focus is on runtime pain points: tail latency, unexpected token costs, model fallbacks, and developer ergonomics for Dedicated/Private customers. This is not a long synthesis — it’s a pragmatic conversion of field vignettes into engineering experiments and customer touchpoints.

How this doc is organized:
- Topline themes (3) with representative vignettes
- Microprobe candidates (6) with hypothesis, quick measurement plan, owner, rough effort, and risk
- Open questions and customer comm plan
- Next steps and backlog plumbs (tickets to create)

Topline themes (summary)
1) Tail latency surprises on medium-length prompts (~512 tokens). Customers with interactive chat workflows observe sporadic spikes when KV cache misses occur, especially after model swaps or small-rollouts to new hosts.
2) Token-cost mismatch: customers report that embeddings + generation combos sometimes double-bill because they run separate routes; confusion on per-token vs per-embedding billing for composite flows.
3) Fallback behavior opacity: when Redwood routes to a cheaper quantized variant, outputs sometimes degrade and customers don’t see an easily consumable trace that explains the change.

Representative vignettes (realized from CS interviews)
- Fintech startup: 'Our helpdesk bot has occasional 800–1200ms spikes after long idle periods. The KV cache looks empty and retries to warm it cause more tokens and time.' (customer thread #JIRA-INT-1803)
- Edtech integrator: 'We batch embeddings on a nightly job then run prompts. Our billing jumped 2x the week we moved to dedicated; we later realized a route duplicated requests for embeddings.' (support convo 2026-07-19)
- Marketplace platform: 'We got a model fallback during a Canary. There was no clear log link; UX showed same model name but different perf. Hard to debug for compliance teams.'

Microprobe candidates (prioritized by expected impact / time to learn)
1) Probe: KV-cache warming telemetry spike detector
   - Hypothesis: Spikes correlate with cold-kv events and can be detected by observing token-latency pattern + cache-miss signal from runtime.
   - Measure: add synthetic marker in perf traces that flags first-regen-after-0-kv hits; track frequency for 1 week across 10 customers.
   - Owner: Li Wei (serving-runtime)
   - Effort: 3d to add marker + 2d to wire dashboard slices in Console
   - Risk: low (read-only telemetry), high debugging ROI

2) Probe: Composite-billing audit for combined embedding+generate flows
   - Hypothesis: Many customers unknowingly hit two billable routes; a simple audit-running script can surface offending patterns and a docs fix will reduce surprise billing incidents by 60%
   - Measure: run script on last 30 days of usage for 20 tenants and surface routes with duplicate token counting
   - Owner: Omar Patel (customer-success) + Finance analyst (ad-hoc)
   - Effort: 4d scripting + 2d comms template
   - Risk: medium (requires access to billing logs, PII-safe sampling)

3) Probe: Transparent fallback trace in Console (first-iteration)
   - Hypothesis: If we show a condensed 'fallback trace' (time, source model, fallback target, perf delta, rollout id), customers can triage regressions faster and reduce escalations.
   - Measure: prototype UI card for 5 customers on Dedicated; measure time-to-resolution on related tickets.
   - Owner: Samira Khan (product console) + eng console-and-tooling
   - Effort: 1 sprint for prototype (MVP card), 1 sprint for backfill
   - Risk: medium (data surface and privacy considerations)

4) Probe: Route-safety lint for SDK usage patterns
   - Hypothesis: Many duplicate requests come from client SDK misuse (creating separate calls vs single composite API). A local lint or CI check can catch common anti-patterns.
   - Measure: ship a beta linter rule to 10 customers; count prevented duplication events in first 30 days.
   - Owner: Developer Experience (TBD) — recommend contact: Rajiv Desai
   - Effort: 1wk rule + docs + sample PRs
   - Risk: low (opt-in developer tooling)

5) Probe: Canary artifact mapping + automatic 'explain-fallback' email trigger
   - Hypothesis: When a Canary triggers a fallback event for a customer, an automated email (or Console alert) with a concise explain-log reduces confusion and support load.
   - Measure: pilot for 3 canaries over 2 weeks; compare ticket volume to baseline.
   - Owner: Platform Engineering / Release Engineering (coord)
   - Effort: 2w small infra + email template work
   - Risk: privacy / opt-out complexity

6) Probe: Cost-simulator microtool for route planners
   - Hypothesis: A tiny interactive sim in Console (input: avg tokens, qps, batching profile) that outputs per-token and per-route cost estimates will prevent poor config choices.
   - Measure: A/B test with 50 Dedicated customers; track change in config churn and tickets about cost surprises.
   - Owner: Product-Optimize + Console
   - Effort: 2w prototype + small UX polish
   - Risk: low (data-driven advisory only)

Open questions (needs answers before full engineering work)
- What telemetry fields are safe to surface in fallback trace without leaking model internals? (security / legal)
- Can billing logs be sampled in a way that preserves tenant anonymity for internal audits? (finance + privacy)
- Which Dedicated customers would accept opt-in canary tracing? (CS to recruit)

Customer comm plan (short and concrete)
- Recruit 6 customers (mix of Dedicated/Hosted) for a 'microprobe alpha' via personal outreach this week (owners: Omar + Samira).
- Send a 1-paragraph 'what we’re testing' note and 2-question consent form (will we surface traces, will we accept a console flag?).
- Weekly status note to participating customers + a short post-mortem with actionable changes.

Immediate next steps (today → 2 weeks)
- Create tracking tickets: CS-MICRO-001..006 (owner labels) — ACTION: Ava to create by EOD 2026-08-04.
- Li to spike KV-cache marker; deliver small trace sample by 2026-08-07.
- Omar to prepare composite-billing script skeleton and request finance access.
- Samira to draft a Console card mock and coordinate with Console eng for feasibility.

Notes to self / heuristics for writing probes
- Keep each probe measurable in ≤2 metrics.
- Prefer telemetry-first probes (fast learning) before UI-heavy solutions.
- Aim for low customer disruption — opt-in alpha is preferred.

Appendix (quick references)
- Short list of relevant tickets and threads: JIRA-INT-1803, JIRA-OPS-993, SUPPORT-2026-07-19.
- Slack thread: #cs-field-harvest (pinned notes 2026-07-22).

If you read this and want to help: reply with which probe you can own (Li/Omar/Samira called out above) and any immediate blockers (access to logs, Console quota).

— Ava
